requests.user: {"source":"We compared three layouts in a small internal exercise: a table, a chart, and a paragraph summary. Each volunteer saw the same set of sample figures and answered two kinds of questions. One asked for an exact value; the other asked what had changed across the sequence. Participants found the table easiest to scan when they needed exact values, while the chart helped them notice broad changes. The paragraph summary prompted useful discussion, but several volunteers returned to the table to confirm a number. We took notes during the exercise rather than recording completion times, so we should not describe any layout as faster. The sample figures were invented for the prototype and did not represent a live service. Because the exercise used only six volunteers from our office, these observations should guide the next prototype rather than support a general claim about all readers. The next round could include people who do not work with these figures every day and could ask them to explain how they reached an answer.
